requirement: The bundled skills MUST direct agents to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows; to use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole; and to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.
rationale:
The subject has three obligations. The bundled skills must direct agents to do each of these:

1. Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites.
2. Use `{impl}` when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole.
3. Mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.

**Implementation.** `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md` is declared as the `:impl:` for this requirement, and it carries all three obligations.
- The intro says distributed requirements are for obligations that "apply on their own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows".
- The first `## Do` bullet covers obligations 1 and 2: "Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each site; when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole, use `{impl}` there."
- The `## Do` bullet "Separate obligations each site upholds from obligations particular code carries out, and mark that code `{impl}`" covers obligation 3.
- The `## Don't` bullet about sites needing no reference says a site that carries out one of the requirement's other obligations "gets `{impl}` of this one like any other root". This reinforces obligation 3.
- The guidance is reachable from the skills. `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` links to the reference, and the bootstrap skill and the evidence skill's `references/reviews.md` also point to it.

**Tests.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_make_a_requirement_distributed_only_for_per_site_obligations]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It reads the `## Do` section of the reference through `section` and `distributed_reference`. Through `assert_text`, it asserts that both bullets are present verbatim. Those two bullets cover all three obligations. The code under test is static text, so the assertion on its content is the right check.

I found no unspecified behavior and no gap.
